_comment: DESIRED GOVERNANCE STATE OF THE REPO. Single source of truth for scripts/gh/apply-governance.sh.
This file does not apply itself: the script compares it against the real state via GET and only mutates with --apply.
Decisions and their rationale are documented in the _why_* fields of each block.
Verified live (GET only) on 2026-08-04 against CristianAjavi/ethical-hacker-squad.
_why_actions_app_id: id of the 'github-actions' GitHub App (verified: gh api /apps/github-actions -> id 15368).
Every required check is pinned to this app. Without app_id, any integration with write access (or a
stolen token) can publish a GREEN commit status with the same 'context' and satisfy the gate without
running anything at all. For a security repo this is mandatory.
_why_settings: allow_auto_merge: auto-merge is NOT a gate, it is a trigger. The option only shows up on PRs that
cannot be merged right away, so the order matters: first the required checks, then
allow_auto_merge=true, and only then 'gh pr merge --auto'. The other way around = instant merge with no gate.
The script enforces that order (it applies main's protection before the settings).
squash-only: linear history and a single commit per PR = a diff auditable per commit, which is what
delete_branch_on_merge: bot/knowledge-* branches delete themselves after merging.
_why_dependabot_security_updates: OFF, and this is a decision rather than a default nobody looked at. It is the one governance
field whose correct value is false, so an unexplained false here reads like drift and would
eventually be 'fixed' by somebody enabling it.
Alerts and security updates are different channels and are easy to confuse: vulnerability_alerts
is REPORTING and is on, this is AUTOMATIC FIXING and is off. Security updates raise pull requests
against every manifest in the dependency graph and, unlike version updates, they are not scoped by
the `updates:` blocks in .github/dependabot.yml - so no directory allowlist keeps them away from
Those trees are answer keys, not dependencies. Nothing installs them. bench/ground-truth.json pins
P-20 by the symbol `lodahs` and P-53 by `svc-token-helpers==1.0.0`, and published runs were scored
against the bytes that are there now. A bot that bumps a pin to fix a CVE edits the fixture under
the measurement, and every number already published stops describing the tree it was measured on.
The cost of leaving it off is real and is accepted: an alert on tooling/claude-cli/** - the one
manifest that is a real dependency, installed by .github/workflows/release.yml - gets no automatic
fix PR. What covers it is the weekly npm version-update block on that directory alone, and a human
reading the alert. scripts/gates/data/alert-surface.json is where a triager is told which is which.

secret_scanning._note: I did NOT verify against official docs that secret scanning + push protection are available via API on a public repo of a personal Free account. The script treats a 4xx here as COULD NOT MEASURE (rc 2), never as success.

_why_security_and_analysis_declared: COMPLETENESS, not preference. Every key GitHub returns in `security_and_analysis` must appear here
with the status we expect, and every key here must come back from the API. A key the API adds and
nobody declares is the failure this block exists for - it is how dependabot_security_updates spent
weeks correct-by-luck with nothing in the repository aware it was a setting at all.
Two of the five were in the same position when this was written and are now decisions:
secret_scanning_non_provider_patterns OFF - it looks for generic credential shapes rather than known
provider formats. bench/cases/** is full of strings written to look like credentials on purpose;
turning it on floods the channel with fixtures and trains a reader to dismiss it, which is the one
outcome that costs a real alert.
secret_scanning_validity_checks OFF - it asks the provider whether a candidate secret is live. On a
repository whose fixtures are fake secrets, that means transmitting our fixture strings to third
parties to be tested. Not a hypothetical privacy question and not worth it for planted data.
The two blocks above carry the same values with the reasoning and the --apply mutation; this map is
the census. gate-governance-contract.sh checks they agree, so the duplication cannot drift apart.
_why_labels: THIS FILE NO LONGER DECLARES LABELS. The single authority for the label taxonomy is
scripts/gh/labels.sh (34 labels), which is what the issue forms, gate-issue-closure.sh and
gate-labels-taxonomy.sh are wired to. Two declarations meant two scripts creating labels on
the same repo, each reporting the other's labels as 'undeclared'.
apply-governance.sh now delegates: it runs 'scripts/gh/labels.sh --check' and folds in its rc.
promotion.blocking_issue_labels below only REFERENCES names from that taxonomy; gate-labels-taxonomy.sh
fails if a name referenced here does not exist there.
_why_promotion: required_contexts: names of the check runs that MUST exist and be conclusion=success on the
candidate commit. A check run is named after the job's 'name:' field, so these two strings must
match the 'name:' of the two jobs in .github/workflows/ci.yml EXACTLY. They are kept short and
identifier-like for that reason. Anti-lockout safeguard: --apply REFUSES to declare a context
never observed in main's recent check runs. Use --discover-contexts to list observed ones.
tag_prefix: the convention `claude plugin tag` expects is <plugin-name>--vX.Y.Z, and
.github/workflows/release.yml validates it with `claude plugin tag --dry-run` before pushing.
It also keeps the tag space of stable separate from any tag on main.
blocking_issue_labels: any OPEN ISSUE (not a PR) carrying one of these stops promotion. The name
must exist in scripts/gh/labels.sh or GitHub silently ignores it and the block is inert;
cooldown_days: the rest window, read by release.yml (single source of truth; the workflow no

_why: CLASSIC protection (PUT /branches/{b}/protection), not a ruleset. Reason: the availability note
for PUBLIC repos on Free is explicit in the branch-protection REST docs, whereas the availability
of REPOSITORY rulesets on a personal Free account is NOT documented (we only have a
GET /rulesets -> 200 [] as a hint). Besides, PUT is a full replacement = idempotent by
construction, which is exactly what you want in a script that runs unattended.
restrictions: null MANDATORY. Quote from the docs: 'User, app, and team restrictions are only
available for organization-owned repositories. Omit this parameter for personal repositories.'
Honest consequence: here you CANNOT express 'only the bot writes to X'. The real guarantee comes
from the executable gates, not from the branch rule.
required_approving_review_count 0: it demands the PR PATH (nothing enters by direct push, everything
goes through checks) without demanding a human approval that nobody can give in a single-owner repo.
require_code_owner_reviews false: see .github/CODEOWNERS, which exists only to route and notify.
enforce_admins false: A CONSCIOUS, DOCUMENTED DECISION. It is the only rollback mechanism left
(GITHUB_TOKEN is not admin and cannot force-push a protected branch). If you set it to true, the
stable rollback documented in release.yml stops working without disabling the protection
by hand. The control here is not the block, it is the audit trail.
checks: this list and promotion.required_contexts must name the SAME contexts. They did not:
workflow-hardening was verified by the promotion and required by nothing, so the job ran on
every pull request and its red blocked no merge (issue #16, finding F-005 of the blinded
self-audit). Adding a context here is what makes it real; declaring it there is what makes it
checked at promotion. gate-governance-contract.sh fails while the two lists disagree, so this
cannot drift back silently. Note what the job does NOT cover, because the verifier narrowed it
and the narrowing travels: it does not detect impostor commits or known-vulnerable actions -
ZIZMOR_ONLINE is never set in ci.yml and those audits live in supply-chain-audit.yml.
stable carries neither a mandatory PR nor required checks, on purpose. The promotion workflow pushes
an already verified SHA directly (git push origin <sha>:refs/heads/stable). A required check on
stable would block that push without adding any guarantee: the verification already happened on the
candidate commit in main.
What IS hardened: allow_force_pushes=false (the history of the channel consumed by plugin users
cannot be rewritten) and allow_deletions=false (the channel cannot be deleted).
A fast-forward push is NOT a force push, so the normal promotion goes through.
Operational reminder: this branch DOES NOT EXIST TODAY. The script cannot protect it until the first
promotion creates it; that is why it reports rc 2 (could not measure) and not rc 0.

_discarded.rulesets: Documented plan B, not implemented. Real advantages (they stack, enforcement=evaluate, /history to audit drift, bypass_actors) but: availability on a personal Free repo UNVERIFIED, there is no upsert endpoint (idempotency has to be built by listing by name), and none of those advantages pay off with one maintainer and one weekly bot. If some day a bypass is needed for a non-human actor, that is the moment to migrate (bypass_actors {actor_type:'Integration', actor_id:15368, bypass_mode:'pull_request'}). Rule: NEVER mix classic protection and a ruleset on the same branch; when they stack the most restrictive wins and a ruleset bypass does not cancel a classic block.
_discarded.merge_queue: Discarded. It solves contention between concurrent PRs, which does not exist here (one maintainer + one weekly bot), and in exchange it adds the merge_group trigger, that is, one more execution surface to audit. Complexity with no benefit.
_discarded.restrictions_push: Impossible on a personal repo (org-only). Not pursued.
_discarded.require_code_owner_reviews: With a single human with write access, it either blocks the owner on their own PRs or reintroduces the human click that automatic promotion is meant to remove.
